arxiv-2109-02145.title: Temporal Shift Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2109-02145.creator: Deepak George Thomas, Tichakorn Wongpiromsarn, Ali Jannesari
arxiv-2109-02145.description: Abstract The function approximators employed by traditional image-based Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms usually lack a temporal learning component and instead focus on learning the spatial component. We propose a technique, Temporal Shift Reinforcement Learning (TSRL), wherein both temporal, as well as spatial components are jointly learned. Moreover, TSRL does not require additional parameters to perform temporal learning.

arxiv-2111-01433.description: Abstract The paper investigates a class of a semilinear wave equation with time-dependent damping term ( − 1 ( 1 + t ) β ​ Δ ​ u t -\frac{1}{{(1+t)}^{\beta}}\Delta u_{t} ) and a nonlinearity | u | p |u|^{p} .

arxiv-2403-04063.title: Assigning Entities to Teams as a Hypergraph Discovery Problem
arxiv-2403-04063.creator: Guilherme Ferraz de Arruda ∗, Wan He ∗, Nasimeh Heydaribeni ∗, Tara Javidi, Yamir Moreno, Tina Eliassi-Rad
arxiv-2403-04063.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Guilherme Ferraz de Arruda ∗, Wan He ∗, Nasimeh Heydaribeni ∗, Tara Javidi, Yamir Moreno, Tina Eliassi-Rad. We propose a team assignment algorithm based on a hypergraph approach focusing on resilience and diffusion optimization. Specifically, our method is based on optimizing the algebraic connectivity of the Laplacian matrix of an edge-dependent vertex-weighted hypergraph. We used constrained simulated annealing, where we constrained the effort agents can exert to perform a task and the minimum effort a task requires to be completed.

arxiv-2407-14992.title: On the strength of Burer’s lifted convex relaxation to quadratic programming with ball constraints
arxiv-2407-14992.creator: Fatma Kılınç-Karzan, Shengding Sun
arxiv-2407-14992.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fatma Kılınç-Karzan, Shengding Sun. We study quadratic programs with m m ball constraints, and the strength of a lifted convex relaxation for it recently proposed by Burer (2024). Burer shows this relaxation is exact when m = 2 m=2 . For general m m , Burer (2024) provides numerical evidence that this lifted relaxation is tighter than the Kronecker product based Reformulation Linearization Technique (RLT) inequalities introduced by Anstreicher (2017), and conjectures that this must be theoretically true as well.

arxiv-2412-07877.title: Score-Optimal Diffusion Schedules
arxiv-2412-07877.creator: Christopher Williams, Andrew Campbell, Arnaud Doucet, Saifuddin Syed, {williams, campbell, doucet, saifuddin.syed}@stats.ox.ac.uk
arxiv-2412-07877.description: Abstract Denoising diffusion models (DDMs) offer a flexible framework for sampling from high dimensional data distributions. DDMs generate a path of probability distributions interpolating between a reference Gaussian distribution and a data distribution by incrementally injecting noise into the data. To numerically simulate the sampling process, a discretisation schedule from the reference back towards clean data must be chosen.

arxiv-2508-08537.title: Training Kindai OCR with parallel textline images and self-attention feature distance-based loss
arxiv-2508-08537.creator: Anh Le, Asanobu Kitamoto
arxiv-2508-08537.description: Abstract Kindai documents, written in modern Japanese from the late 19th to early 20th century, hold significant historical value for researchers studying societal structures, daily life, and environmental conditions of that period. However, transcribing these documents remains a labor-intensive and time-consuming task, resulting in limited annotated data for training optical character recognition (OCR) systems.

arxiv-2511-00940.title: URDF-Anything: Constructing Articulated Objects with 3D Multimodal Language Model
arxiv-2511-00940.creator: Zhe Li, Xiang Bai, Jieyu Zhang, Zhuangzhe Wu, Che Xu, Ying Li, Chengkai Hou, Shanghang Zhang, Science, Peking University, University of Washington
arxiv-2511-00940.description: Abstract Constructing accurate digital twins of articulated objects is essential for robotic simulation training and embodied AI world model building, yet historically requires painstaking manual modeling or multi-stage pipelines. In this work, we propose URDF-Anything , an end-to-end automatic reconstruction framework based on a 3D multimodal large language model (MLLM).

pmc-11471780.title: Aptamer-drug conjugates-loaded bacteria for pancreatic cancer synergistic therapy
pmc-11471780.creator: Yu Xiao, Tao Pan, Wuren Da, Yuanding Liu, Shuangya Chen, Daiquan Chen, Keying Liu, Yihan Zheng, Daolong Xie, Yuan Gao, Haiyan Xu, Yang Sun, Weihong Tan
pmc-11471780.description: Pancreatic cancer is one of the most malignant tumors with the highest mortality rates, and it currently lacks effective drugs. Aptamer-drug conjugates (ApDC), as a form of nucleic acid drug, show great potential in cancer therapy. However, the instability of nucleic acid-based drugs in vivo and the avascularity of pancreatic cancer with dense stroma have limited their application.

pmc-11689969.title: MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT OF SOCIAL DISCONNECTION IN OLDER ADULTS AT HEIGHTENED RISK FOR SUICIDE
pmc-11689969.creator: Emily Bower, Taylor Loskot, Kimberly Van Orden
pmc-11689969.description: Social disconnection is a proximal and modifiable risk factor for suicide among older adults. Identifying periods of acute or intensified disconnection can inform just-in-time interventions for individuals at heightened risk for suicide. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) using mobile devices is feasible and acceptable for older adults, and is a promising method for capturing daily changes in social disconnection.

pmc-12422813.title: The renal baroreflex: A systematic review and meta‐analysis in healthy and hypertensive animals
pmc-12422813.creator: Maaike van Ochten, Wisal El Fathi, Esmee M. E. Bovee, Marc E. A. Spaanderman, Carlijn R. Hooijmans, Joris van Drongelen
pmc-12422813.description: The renal baroreflex describes the dose‐dependent relation between renal pressure and renin release. Former studies have approximated this relation through animal experiments, but the exact shape of the response curve and its alteration by hypertension remain unclear. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review and meta‐analysis on the renal baroreflex in healthy and hypertensive animals.

pmc-12621151.title: Key Action Areas for Population and Planetary Health: Recommendations Arising From the Transforming the UK Food Systems Programme
pmc-12621151.creator: Emma Hunter, Tracey Duncombe, Alexandra Johnstone, Hannah Mitchell, Roya Shahrokni, Riaz Bhunnoo, Guy Poppy
pmc-12621151.description: The UK food system faces critical challenges at the intersection of public health, environmental sustainability, and economic resilience. Currently contributing significantly to greenhouse gas emissions, biodiversity loss, and freshwater use, the system also fails to ensure universal access to healthy diets—particularly for lower‐income populations during a cost‐of‐living crisis.

pmc-12626745.title: No Effects of rTMS on Performance Monitoring and Attentional Bias in Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder: A Pilot Study
pmc-12626745.creator: Maarten Belgers, Wiebren Markus, Federico Grasso, Martijn Arns, Philip Van Eijndhoven, Arnt Schellekens
pmc-12626745.description: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) presents a promising approach for treating patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD). However, its neuropsychological working mechanisms are to be elucidated. Therefore, we investigated the effect of rTMS treatment on event‐related potentials (ERPs) evoked by a flanker task and a passive picture task using electro‐encephalography, in 30 recently detoxified patients.

pmc-13205149.title: Comparative Performance Analysis of Commercial SARS-CoV-2 RNA Detection Assays: Implications for Sensitivity, Specificity, Accuracy, and Diagnostic Response Time
pmc-13205149.creator: Adriana Guimarães dos Santos, José Rodrigo Santos Silva, Maria Luísa Rodrigues Nolasco, Marcus Vinicius de Aragão Batista
pmc-13205149.description: Background/Objectives: In 2020, the world found itself in the midst of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. The virus has spread globally, resulting in over 779 million cases worldwide. In response to this crisis, there arose a critical need for diagnostic techniques capable of meeting the overwhelming global demand, including RT-qPCR as the gold standard due to its high sensitivity and specificity.

pmc-13409635.title: Concentration, Information, and Distributional Stability in High-Dimensional Portfolios: A Talagrand Stability Index Approach
pmc-13409635.creator: Irina Georgescu, Jani Kinnunen
pmc-13409635.description: This paper investigates the stability of high-dimensional financial portfolios using concentration inequalities, information-theoretic measures, optimal transport metrics, and financial network analysis. Asset returns are generated under both multivariate Gaussian and multivariate Student-t distributions. Equal Weight and Regularized Minimum Variance portfolios are evaluated across alternative portfolio dimensions.
